title: Truncation error and long paths
statement: Let $T$ be a real-valued decision tree on the Boolean cube, let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, and suppose every value of $T$ is either $-1$ or $1$. For each input $x$, the squared difference between the value of $T$ at $x$ and the value of the tree obtained by truncating at depth $k$ and assigning value $0$ at newly created leaves is at most the number of root-to-leaf paths of length greater than $k$ whose coordinate assignments agree with $x$.
hypotheses_covered: A decision tree on the Boolean cube with real-valued leaves
Every input is evaluated by $T$ to either $-1$ or $1$
The input $x$ lies in the Boolean cube
